agent: Claude Code (CLAUDE.md, this repository) — WP-02 step 2 of 5
summary_for_principal: Made the engine actually run something for the first time: a single step of a process, for the kind of step that is deterministic (plain code, not an AI model or a person). Before it runs, it checks permission; if the step's output doesn't meet the quality bar the format requires, it says so rather than pretending it passed. While building this, found a real hole in the new format itself: it required checking permission before running anything, but never said which field on a step actually names the permission needed. Added that field and wrote up the decision, the same way earlier gaps were handled. Also found that many real steps declare more than one quality check, and this engine can currently only actually run one specific kind of check — so those steps correctly refuse to run for now rather than being let through only partly checked. Nothing changes for existing definitions; this is additive.

decisions.headline: A Tool's dispatch permission is an optional, opaque `permission` field (D12); absent means refuse to dispatch.
decisions.problem: engine/steps.py's permission check (S10.1) needs a concrete string to pass to PolicyPort.authorize(), and nothing in the format as drafted names where that string comes from.
options_rejected: Derive a permission string automatically from the Tool's own id (e.g. `<tool-id>.dispatch`): rejected — invents a naming scheme ADR-024 reserves to the host; two hosts would derive two different strings from the same Tool, defeating the point of the host owning its own grammar.

Make `permission` a required field on every Tool now, enforced by the JSON Schema: rejected for this draft — would invalidate every Tool fixture already written against v1 (WP-01's Appendix A corpus included), a large, unrelated blast radius for a field this decision can add without it.

An optional field that, absent, means dispatch proceeds unchecked: rejected — silently defeats S10.1's own "before it dispatches any Tool", exactly the bad-but-conformant path this format's principles ask every rule to defeat.
decisions.cost_to_change: Tightening `permission` to schema-required is additive once fixtures are updated to declare it; the engine-side refusal-on-absence rule is local to engine/steps.py and can be relaxed in one place.

evidence.claim: No `permission` field exists anywhere on Tool in model.py or tool.v1.schema.json before this PR; grep for "permission" in the spec turns up only the gate decider's `person.permission` and the trigger-permission and D5 ("permission is checked") mentions, never a Tool-level field.
evidence.source: docs/spec/process-definition.md, grepped directly this session; src/sulis_workflows/definition/model.py and schema/tool.v1.schema.json, read directly.

load_bearing_assumptions: No Tool fixture in this repository currently declares a `permission` field under a different name that this decision would collide with — verified false collision risk by grepping the Appendix A corpus, which has no such field anywhere.
decisions.revisit_if: A future WP-01-style validator PR adds a rule requiring `permission` on every Tool, at which point every fixture needs updating together.

decisions.headline: Controls-checking is scoped to `profile:` controls only for this PR; a Tool with any `conventions:`/`fitness:`/`policy:` control refuses to dispatch.
decisions.problem: S10.2 requires every non-policy control's checker to run after a step. This engine has no way to call a `conventions:`/`fitness:` control's checker Tool generically yet (no fixture or built-in defines one as a real callable), and S10.2 doesn't specify a runtime path for `policy:`-kind Tool controls at all (only GATE's `policy` decider is specified, S7.6).
options_rejected: Treat an uncheckable control as passed by default so more real Tools can run: rejected — this is exactly the bad-but-conformant path CLAUDE.md's own principles name: a control that is never actually checked is indistinguishable, from the outside, from one that always passes.

Build a generic checker-Tool dispatch path now (resolve the Control's `.checker` Tool via Registry and call it through CodeToolPort) even though no such checker exists in any fixture yet: rejected — speculative against a shape nothing has exercised; the two real built-in checkers (profile_conformance, decision_evidence) have bespoke signatures, not a generic (inputs: dict) -> dict shape, so a generic dispatch path would need to be redesigned once a real second checker appears anyway.
decisions.cost_to_change: Additive — a later PR can widen `check_controls` to dispatch more checker kinds without changing this PR's `profile:` path.

evidence.claim: checkers.py implements exactly two checkers: profile_conformance(value, control, *, registry) and decision_evidence(value, control, reviewing) — different signatures from each other and from a generic Tool-dispatch shape; decision_evidence is specific to gate decisions (S7.6), not a STEP control.

The Appendix A corpus's own interrogate.tool.yaml declares both a `profile:` control and a `conventions:` control together on the same Tool — confirming real Tools mix checkable and (currently) unchecked kinds, so partial trust would be a real, not hypothetical, gap.

decisions.revisit_if: A real `conventions:`/`fitness:` checker Tool is added to any fixture corpus, giving this engine something concrete to dispatch against.

decisions.headline: A new CodeToolPort, not the existing ToolDispatchPort, dispatches a CODE Tool's `module:function` ref.
decisions.problem: Whether to reuse the deprecated compiler's existing ToolDispatchPort (domain/ports/tool_dispatch.py) for calling a CODE-kind Tool's mechanism.
options_rejected: Reuse ToolDispatchPort's `invoke(primitive, args, *, sandbox_root, ...)` generic escape hatch: rejected — `sandbox_root` is a mandatory keyword argument tied to that port's workspace-primitive concern (read_file/glob/ripgrep for a sandboxed filesystem); a CODE Tool's dotted `module:function` ref has no workspace path to supply, so every call site would need to invent a meaningless placeholder just to satisfy the signature.
decisions.cost_to_change: The two ports could be merged later if ToolDispatchPort's shape changes to make sandbox_root optional; nothing in this PR depends on them staying separate.

evidence.claim: ToolDispatchPort.invoke requires `sandbox_root: WorkspacePath` as a non-optional keyword argument on every call, per its own Protocol definition and docstring ("Every method carries sandbox_root (NFR-14)").
evidence.source: src/sulis_workflows/domain/ports/tool_dispatch.py, read in full this session and in a prior turn.

decisions.revisit_if: Never expected to need reversing — the two ports serve genuinely different concerns (workspace primitives vs. arbitrary CODE Tool dispatch).

lessons.destination: Any future PR in this repository building runtime logic against the definition/ model — check the Appendix A corpus fixtures before assuming a field's runtime meaning from its schema type alone.
